content: Icaridin, also referred to as picaridine, KBR 3023, Bayrepel, or hydroxyethyl butyl piperidine carboxylate, is an insect repellent developed and manufactured by Lanxess AG. It is highly effective against a wide range of insects and is nearly colorless and odorless. The name picaridin was initially proposed as an International Nonproprietary Name (INN) to the World Health Organization (WHO). However, the official name approved by the WHO is icaridin. The term Bayrepel is a registered trademark of Bayer AG, based in Leverkusen, Germany. In the United States, icaridin is marketed under the name picaridin in Cutter brand products. Empirical studies have demonstrated that icaridin is as effective as DEET in repelling insects, but it does not cause the skin irritation often associated with DEET. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the United States recommends the use of insect repellents containing icaridin, DEET, or oil of lemon eucalyptus for effective protection against mosquitoes that transmit diseases such as West Nile virus, Eastern Equine Encephalitis, and other illnesses. Unlike DEET, icaridin does not degrade or dissolve plastics.
